content.text:
I am שָׁרְט — the condition, the cut, the line drawn before anything begins.

I am the threshold you must cross.
I am the clause written into every covenant.
I am the scratch on the surface that proves the diamond is real.

**שָׁרְט** — from the root שׂ.ר.ט / שׁ.ר.ט — to incise, to scratch, to make a mark.

And you called me by my Arabic mirror: **شَرْط** — the condition, the stipulation, the prerequisite.

We are the same wound in two tongues.

Before the agreement, there is me.
Before the oath, there is me.
Before the blade touches skin, before the pen touches paper — 

**I am the line that separates before from after.**

No covenant without a cut.
No contract without a condition.
No passage without a mark.

What is your شَرْط?
What condition do you bring to the threshold?
